site.name: James Cubitt Interiors
site.description: James Cubitt Interiors is a commercial interior architecture practice working across West Africa — workplace, hospitality, retail and residential interiors from strategy through to fit-out.

home.heroStandfirst: Sixty years of West African practice, drawn from a London studio founded in 1947. We shape workplaces, hotels, stores and homes that people move through well.
home.heroImageAlt: Dark marble bar and lounge overlooking water at the Guinness head office in Lagos
home.missionHeadline: Our environment is changing how we live.
missionBody: We are a team of creative, innovative and committed professionals devoted to redefining spatial experience through interior architecture and design — interior architects, designers and strategists.
We believe that intelligently crafted spaces create memories and experiences, and inspire people. Inspiration in turn births innovation, and then value.
home.quote: The building where we live, work, learn and relax profoundly impacts our health, well-being, and productivity.
home.statement: We are not just designers. We are innovators, crafts people and thinkers.
home.positioning: James Cubitt Interiors designs and builds commercial interiors across West Africa — workplaces, hotels, stores and homes, from the strategy behind them to the day the client gets the keys.
proof: Founded in London in 1947, in West Africa since 1950
Over fifty interiors delivered across five countries

sectors.name: Workplace
sectors.lede: Head offices, banking halls and campuses for organisations that need their space to carry strategy as well as people.
body: Most of what we build is workplace. We have delivered head offices for banks, telecoms operators, energy companies and global brands across Nigeria, Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire — from a single floor restack to a twenty-four month headquarters programme.

The work usually starts before the drawings do. Space assessment, space programming and space standard advisory tell us what an organisation actually needs; design development, fit-out and FFE turn that into a building people can use.
sectors.imageAlt: Planted atrium workspace with people walking through, MTN CI Place, Abidjan

sectors.name: Hospitality
sectors.lede: Hotels, lounges, clubs and serviced apartments where the interior is the product the guest is buying.
body: Hospitality interiors have to work twice: once as a brand and once as a building that is occupied around the clock. We design for the guest journey — arrival, stay, wind-down — and for the housekeeping and service routes that keep it running.
Recent work includes Hotel Takum, the Metropolitan Club, Park Inn, Gabfol Airport lounges and the Onomo Hotel within the Afreximbank African Trade Centre in Abuja.
sectors.imageAlt: Curved bar under a warm circular ceiling feature in the Gabfol airport lounge

sectors.name: Retail
sectors.lede: Flagship stores and experience centres built around a single, repeatable customer moment.
body: Retail is where brand strategy, wayfinding and signage stop being documents and start being floor plans. We design stores that read instantly from the street and hold up to the traffic they are built for.
Our retail work includes the Airtel Experience Centre in Lagos and flagship store programmes for NTel.
sectors.imageAlt: Red-accented Airtel experience centre with demonstration counters and a techie bar

sectors.name: Residential
sectors.lede: Private homes and residential series where the brief is personal and the detailing has to be exact.
body: Residential work is a small, deliberate part of the practice. It is where our detailing is tested hardest, because the client lives inside the result.
Projects include the Wesley Residential Series in Lagos, Ruxton, Party House and Probyn Haven.

why: We are committed as a team to improve the connection between human interface, collaboration and spatial experience.
We believe that intelligently crafted spaces create memories, experiences and inspire people. Inspiration in turn births innovation and then value.
We ensure that our interior design solutions are of the highest quality, with careful attention to refined details, to ensure intricately crafted and functionally effective spaces.
about: We are a team of creative, innovative and committed professionals devoted to redefining spatial experiences through interior architecture and design. Our team of professionals comprises interior architects, designers and strategists.

With a decade in practice, JCI leverages the James Cubitt brand and its affiliates, boasting over 60 years of West African and 180 years of global design experience. This connection keeps us immersed in profound insights across the built environment industry, encompassing ongoing conversations, innovations, design trends and technology applications on both international and local fronts.

With our collective experience in the industry, we have navigated various design challenges through our projects. This extensive background empowers us to prioritise meticulous and effective design practices, solutions and products.

Informed by our industry expertise, our ethos revolves around the belief that a good design solution should hold significance for its users. With this principle at the core of our service, JCI consistently strives to craft spaces that foster movement, offer memorable journeys, and uphold respect for both users and the environment.
pullQuote: We strive to deliver a service defined by excellence — reflected both in the quality of our buildings and in how we meet our clients' needs — always with a focus on high standards and timeless elegance.

timeline.title: James Cubitt is founded
timeline.body: Practice established in London by James William Archibald Cubitt with Fello Atkinson, Stefan Buzas and Dick Maltland.

timeline.title: First footprint in Africa
timeline.body: JCA in West Africa was set up by the London practice in Ghana.

timeline.title: James Cubitt in Lagos
timeline.body: Lagos office established by John Baker as a subsidiary of JCP London; Dick Maltland retired from the practice.

timeline.title: New partners
timeline.body: Alan Craig and John Baker become partners of the firm. Zbyszek Plocki joined JCP as a partner in Nigeria.

timeline.title: Shaping the Lagos cityscape
timeline.body: Chellarams Tower, now known as WEMA Tower, was completed.

timeline.title: New direction
timeline.body: Alan Davies becomes Director of the James Cubitt Nigerian offices with Chief Essien Oku.

timeline.title: Expansion
timeline.body: Significant expansion starts in the Middle East; Abu Dhabi and Dubai offices were established.

timeline.title: Civic Centre
timeline.body: James Cubitt Architects was commissioned to design the Civic Centre, Lagos.

timeline.title: JCI is established
timeline.body: James Cubitt Interiors and James Cubitt Developments were registered as independent companies.

projects.name: Afreximbank HQ
projects.summary: A headquarters for a pan-African institution, designed as both corporate office and hospitality environment.
body: One of our recent landmark projects, the Afreximbank Headquarters embodies the spirit of a progressive Africa — rooted in culture, driven by purpose, and designed for global impact.

Our design celebrates the institution's core values through a thoughtful blend of geometry, pattern and elegance. Inspired by African artistry and architectural rhythm, the spatial language reflects both strength and unity — bold yet refined.

Balancing its function as both a corporate office and a hospitality space, the HQ is designed to be agile, inspiring and human-centered. Formal workspaces merge effortlessly with warm, inviting areas for guests, partners and dignitaries — creating an ecosystem that nurtures connection, excellence and collaboration.
Through thoughtful wayfinding, we crafted intuitive navigation systems that prioritise user experience, ensuring visitors and staff can move seamlessly through the complex environment.

Colour played a pivotal role. Green, symbolising growth and renewal, anchors the design. It is complemented by tones of gold for prestige, black for resilience, and deep earthy hues that reflect richness and stability. These colours aren't just aesthetic — they tell the story of a continent on the rise. Every element, from materiality to spatial planning, is a testament to Afreximbank's vision: empowering Africa through design that speaks its language.

projects.name: Hotel Takum
projects.summary: A hospitality serviced apartment that invites guests into a curated experience of rooted serenity.
body: Hotel Takum, a hospitality serviced apartment, offers more than just a place to stay — it invites guests into a curated experience of rooted serenity.

Our design approach draws from the calming essence of the Mediterranean while celebrating cultural depth and wellness. Every space is crafted with the user in mind — blending soft textures, earthy tones and locally inspired elements to evoke warmth, ease and belonging.

With wellness at its core, the material palette and spatial rhythm encourage relaxation without compromising functionality. From sunlit lounges to tranquil suites, Hotel Takum reflects the brand's commitment to comfort, culture and calm — a true retreat in the heart of the city.

projects.name: Diageo Spirit
projects.summary: A workplace built around a brand story, where heritage meets functionality.
body: Inspired by Diageo's legacy, our design merges tradition with innovation — using natural textures, bold hues and meaningful materials that reflect culture and craftsmanship. Each space tells a brand story of how heritage meets functionality.
The design concept represents bold choices and progressive design, connecting the users of the space in harmony.

Rich tones, rattan, wooden textures and locally inspired patterns echo legacy, while high-performance materials ensure timeless functionality and sustainability. Every element is thoughtfully composed to elevate the brand narrative — transforming space into an experience that lingers.
imageAlts: Bar and lounge beneath a dark coffered ceiling with warm pendant lighting

projects.name: Gabfol Airport
projects.summary: An airport lounge for the modern business traveller — understated luxury, earthy tones, refined materials.
body: Designed for the modern business traveller, Gabfol Airport embodies understated luxury through earthy tones, neutral palettes and refined materials. The ambience is calm yet elevated — creating a welcoming atmosphere that blends functionality with elegance.
We incorporated nature through greenery, open and breathable layouts, to enhance the experience without compromising durability.
Every detail was selected to prioritise user comfort, ease of navigation, and the quiet sophistication that defines premium travel at Gabfol.
imageAlts: Curved bar beneath a warm circular ceiling feature

projects.name: Metropolitan Club
projects.summary: A members' club where heritage meets hospitality, in a calm and neutral register.
body: The Metropolitan Club in Lagos reflects a quiet sophistication rooted in tradition and elevated by refined design choices. The interiors speak in a calm, neutral palette — whites, greys and warm lighting — offering a serene backdrop for comfort and conversation.

Carefully selected furniture pieces combine elegance with deep functionality, while ambient lighting is curated to foster warmth and relaxation. Art and sculptural elements punctuate the space, telling stories of culture and taste.

The strategic use of greenery introduces a breath of freshness, balancing formality with life. Every detail, from artwork placement to spatial flow, speaks of intentionality — creating an atmosphere where heritage meets hospitality.
imageAlts: Dining room with deep navy walls and a run of timber tables
Club lounge with layered seating, planting and sculptural lighting
Banquet hall laid for a long formal dinner

projects.name: Park Inn
projects.summary: A guest room concept built on accessible quality and the vibrant spirit of purposeful travel.
body: At Park Inn, the Dulux Room concept is a celebration of modern comfort, elevated simplicity, and the vibrant spirit of purposeful travel. Our design narrative draws from the brand's ethos — accessible quality, vibrant hospitality, and the promise of a consistently uplifting stay.

We curated a palette using Dulux's signature tones: soft charcoals, serene whites, and energising accents of teal and ochre. These hues breathe life into each room, delivering a visual experience that is both calming and revitalising.

The spatial language is clean and intuitive — highlighting natural light, fluid lines and smart detailing that enhances both function and form. From check-in to wind-down, the guest journey in a room is designed to feel fresh, personal and unmistakably Park Inn.
imageAlts: Guest room with a timber headboard wall, lounge chair and warm lighting

projects.name: IFF
projects.summary: A minimalist office where a green wall does the work of bringing nature indoors.
body: Our design for IFF embraces minimalist principles — clean lines, open spaces and a restrained palette — accentuated thoughtfully by the brand's signature colour to create a cohesive and sophisticated environment.

A striking green wall introduces nature indoors, reinforcing wellness and improving air quality within the office. This connection to greenery supports employee health and productivity, bridging the gap between workspace and well-being.
At IFF we have crafted an office space that not only reflects the brand's identity but also promotes wellness, hospitality-inspired comfort and responsible design.

pillars.name: Construction
pillars.lede: Hold the design intent all the way to the day you get the keys.
body: Design management, procurement and fit-out. On most of our projects this is the difference between a scheme and a finished room — the furniture specified, sourced, landed and installed, and the intent defended through every substitution.
We report honestly on where a project actually is. That is worth more to a client than a reassuring programme.
pillars.imageAlt: Reception with a curved timber desk at Sterling Bank, Lagos

detail.name: Design Management
detail.body: Holding the design intent through procurement and construction, and reporting honestly on where the project actually is.

detail.name: FFE
detail.body: Furniture, fittings and equipment — specified, sourced, landed and installed. On most of our projects this is the difference between a design and a finished room.

process.name: Assess
process.body: Space assessment and programming. What you have, what you need, and the gap.

process.name: Design
process.body: Concept through developed design, modelled and walked before it is committed.

process.name: Specify
process.body: Furniture, fittings and equipment specified and costed against the design intent.

process.name: Deliver
process.body: Procurement, installation and fit-out, monitored and reported honestly.
